overview:
Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt, the long-serving incumbent, is seeking another term and has built a commanding financial position, raising about $1.0 million with roughly $750,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek has raised about $15,600 and reported just $396 in cash, leaving her little capacity to communicate with voters.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put the chance of a Democratic win near one percent. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and the money gap — all point in the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, Aderholt is positioned to win re-election by a wide margin, and this contest ranks among the least competitive House races on the ballot this fall.
